text:
Ava (PM): Hey team — dropping the PRD draft for the launch gate around audit + crypto controls. link: https://redwood.internal/prd/crypto-audit-evidence

Ava (PM): Main ask: we need concrete acceptance criteria for audit logs (content, retention, access), KMS vs HSM requirements per deployment mode, and what evidence Product can attach for SOC2/ISO sign-off. Can folks weigh-in? :folded_hands:

Rina (Security): skimmed — nice layout. A few quick questions:
- Do audit logs need to be tamper-evident (append-only + signed)?
- Will logs include token-level cost breakdowns or just event-level metadata?
- For Private (on-prem/VPC) do we mandate HSM for key material or allow customer-managed KMS?

Liam (Eng): Re: logs — we can emit structured events that include request id, model, route, token counts, and key-id (not the key). Token-level cost breakdown is heavier but doable as an opt-in field; default should be aggregate to avoid exposing sensitive prompt content.

Marco (SRE): Operationally we need retention and rolloff policies. SRE prefers default 90 days for hosted, with configurable longer retention for Dedicated/Private. Also need a safe delete process for GDPR/erasure requests.

Priya (Legal): For SOC2 we need evidence of log integrity, access controls, and retention policy enforcement. For ISO, also need key custody statements. If logs could contain PII, they need redaction or clear processing docs.

Rina (Security): Proposal: make tamper-evidence mandatory for hosted and dedicated. For Private: allow either customer-managed KMS/HSM or Redwood HSM — but require proof (attestation) if customer uses own HSM.

Ava (PM): That sounds reasonable. Can we boil this into acceptance criteria bullets we can add to PRD? Something machine-checkable for the launch checklist.

Liam (Eng): Draft acceptance criteria snippet (suggested):
```
- Audit logs emitted for all inference requests: fields = request_id, ts, user_id (hashed), model, route, latency_ms, tokens_input, tokens_output, billing_key_id
- Logs are append-only and signed (server-side) for Hosted/Dedicated
- Default retention: 90 days (hosted). Configurable up to 3 years for Dedicated/Private
- Support on-demand PII redaction and data-erasure hooks per request-id
- KMS: Envelope encryption with key_id metadata. HSM-backed keys required for customer requests marked "HSM_required"
- Audit evidence exportable in CSV/JSON and accessible via Console with RBAC and time-range filters
```

Marco (SRE): +1. Add: rotation policy for service keys (90 days) and documented recovery drills. Also, retention exceptions must be logged and require approval.

Rina (Security): Edge cases: cached KV entries in runtime (prefix caching) — do we need to log cache hits that may reveal prompt prefixes? I think log-only cache miss/hit counters, not content.

Liam (Eng): Agreed. We should NOT log prompt text. Log sizes explode otherwise. For embeddings/rerank we can log feature hashes instead of raw content.

Priya (Legal): Regarding export for audits: we need a signed manifest of exported evidence. Also need to confirm chain-of-custody when handing logs to auditors. Add that to acceptance list.

Ava (PM): Nice. Quick callout: Customer asks for "7-year retention" for some regulated customers. Product decision: support via Dedicated/Private with additional storage cost + compliance review. Not supported on Hosted by default.

Rina (Security): HSM/attestation flow: if customer claims HSM, require an attestation doc + periodic re-attestation. For Hosted, Redwood-managed HSM must be FIPS 140-2 TD level 2+ (or current standard).

Liam (Eng): Implementation note: we'll tag logs with `key_access_mode: redwood|customer` and `key_type: kms|hsm` so queries/filters can be used for audit evidence. Sample: `\{"key_access_mode":"redwood","key_type":"hsm"\}`

Marco (SRE): For launch SLOs: emitting logs must not increase  p95 latency > 5ms. We should benchmark. If signing is expensive, do async signing pipeline with write-ahead to ensure append-only semantics.

Ava (PM): Can Eng + SRE draft a short acceptance test matrix we can run in staging and attach results to the PRD? E.g., test cases for tamper-evidence, retention expiry, export manifest, redaction, key rotation.

Liam (Eng): Yep. I'll put a minimal test matrix in the PRD repo tonight. Example rows: `emit_log`, `verify_signature`, `simulate_rotation`, `export_manifest` with pass/fail criteria.

Rina (Security): I'll add the attestation checklist and a minimal SOC2 evidence pack requirements doc.

Priya (Legal): I'll draft the language for customer contracts re: retention overages and evidence requests. Also what we can/can't include in exported logs for privacy reasons.

deploy-bot: CI test run started for branch prd/crypto-audit-evidence (build 5728) — https://ci.redwood.internal/builds/5728 :construction:

Ava (PM): Plan: incorporate these bullets into PRD by EOD, follow-up with staging test matrix, and run one joint review next Wed. Action items: Ava will update PRD; Liam + Marco test matrix; Rina evidence pack; Priya contract text.

Ava (PM): final quick checklist to add to PRD (to be machine-checked if possible):
```
- logs_emitted: true
- tamper_evident: true
- retention_default_days: 90
- retention_configurable: true
- hsm_attestation_required_for_customer_hsm: true
- export_evidence_signed: true
- privacy_redaction_policy: attached
```

Rina (Security): acked. I'll review the exact signing algorithm (RSA vs ECDSA) and propose one.

Liam (Eng): will have test matrix draft by EOD.

Marco (SRE): I'll benchmark signing latency and propose async fallback if needed.

Priya (Legal): will circulate contract language by tomorrow.

Ava (PM): thanks everyone — this was super helpful. I'll update the PRD and ping for review. :rocket:
